lines.meet: I'm Imelda, and I heal by hitting things, and yes, I know how it looks. Stay behind me and you'll feel it when I land one.
lines.meet_neighbour: Freewind Post, right, you're up there too. I'm the one by the lifts, and I'm Imelda.
lines.ask_home: So which part of the world are you from? Keep it short, I'm wrapping my hands.
lines.ask_work: Before this, what kind of work did you do? I can usually tell from the hands.
lines.answer_home: Navotas, in Manila, a fishing district. Same six streets my whole life, and I liked them.
lines.answer_work: I sold fish on the quay from five in the morning, and I boxed in the evenings, about ten fights a year.
lines.chat_food: Grilled fish on the quay, straight off the boat, with rice and a bit of vinegar. My mother's is the best, and she'd tell you so.
lines.chat_sleep: I'm up at five every day, quay hours, even here. My body doesn't know any other time.
lines.chat_missing: The gym above the tyre shop, smelling of sweat and rubber. Nobody here knows how to hit a bag properly.
lines.chat_here: Everybody here fights, but nobody fights properly, with rules and a count. I keep asking, and they keep getting excited about something else.
lines.tease_quiet: You and me could go a whole fight without a word, {name}. I like that in a corner.
lines.tease_talker: You'd talk through the whole bout, {name}, and the ref would throw you out, and I'd laugh.
lines.tease_careful: All jab and no cross with you, {name}. Safe, sure, but you've got to commit sometime.
lines.tease_bold: No guard at all, {name}, you'd be on the canvas in the first round. I'd still bet on you.
lines.tease_any: Your footwork's terrible, {name}. I'll fix it, and I'll enjoy it.
lines.tease_back: Ha, nice shot, {name}, I didn't see that one coming.
lines.take_it_kindly: Okay, you got me there, {name}, that's a fair hit.
lines.bristle: Don't go there, {name}. That's below the belt.
lines.apologise: That was a low blow, and I'm sorry. I don't fight dirty, and I shouldn't talk dirty either.
lines.double_down: That was a clean hit and I'm not taking it back.
lines.needle_quiet: You never tell your corner anything, so nobody can help you. That's how you lose.
lines.needle_talker: You talk so much you forget to breathe. Save it for after the bell.
lines.needle_careful: You keep circling and never throw anything. At some point you've got to hit.
lines.needle_bold: You swing wild and leave yourself wide open, and you call it fighting. I'd call it hoping.
lines.needle_any: You fight dirty when you think nobody's watching. I'm always watching.
lines.bite_back: I've been hit by people who knew how to hit. You don't scare me.
lines.hurt: Okay, that one landed, I felt it. Give me a minute in my corner.
lines.laugh_off: My mother called my whole life a phase for nineteen years. You'll have to do better than her.
lines.confide: {name}, my mother came to exactly one of my fights in nineteen years, and I lost it. She didn't say anything on the way home. I still think about that walk.
lines.listen: I hear you, {name}. That stays in my corner and nobody else's.
lines.look_out: Stay behind me in there, {name}, and watch my back foot. When I move, you move.
lines.accept: Okay, {name}, you're calling the rounds this time.
lines.deflect: It's a scratch, {name}, I've had worse from sparring. Look after the others.
lines.check_in: Up, {name}, slowly, and look at me. What's hurt, and how bad?
lines.blame: Somebody threw a wild one in there and left us all open. I saw who.
lines.thank: I was down, and you got me up before the count. Thank you, really.
lines.brush_off: No big deal, that's what corners are for. Just breathe for me.
lines.worry: Sit down and breathe with me, {name}. I won't lie, that one scared me.
lines.handed_down: I've got your gear on now. I'll keep it clean, like my wraps.
lines.hand_fine: Take it, I'm fine. I've got my hands, and they're enough.
lines.hand_sulk: So it went without anybody asking. I'm not happy about it.
lines.turn_friendly: You're in my corner now, {name}. I don't let many people in there.
lines.turn_friends: I'd let you wrap my hands, {name}. Nobody's ever done it tight enough, and I'd still let you.
lines.turn_grating: We're a bad matchup, you and me. That happens in boxing too.
lines.turn_rivals: I'll still heal you, because it's my job, but don't expect me to like it.
lines.make_up: Touch gloves, {name}? Let's start the bout again, clean this time.
lines.defend: That's a cheap shot, and it isn't true. Back off from {name}.
lines.friend_left: My corner's empty with {name} away, and I don't like it.
lines.friend_back: Good to see you back, {name}. Let's get to work.
lines.common_ring: Nineteen years in the ring, about ten fights a year, and I won more than I lost. Fighters stand a certain way, and you stand like one.
lines.common_sport: I trained every evening after the quay for nineteen years. Anybody who's competed knows the work nobody sees is the real fight.
